title: Screen Self-Service for Jira
body:
For Jira admins and project admins. Find out what Screen Self-Service for Jira does, who it is for, and where to start.

Every screen change shows a preview first and can be undone.

Project admins manage their own Jira screens. Safely.

In company-managed Jira projects, only Jira admins can change screens. A project admin who needs one more field on the create screen files a ticket and waits. Screen Self-Service for Jira lets project admins change the screens that belong to their project alone. Screens shared with other projects stay locked, with the reason shown. Every change shows a preview first, is written to an audit log, and can be undone.

How it works

From setup to everyday use in four steps.

What you can do

 #FFF4EE :eyes:

See every screen at a glance

The Issue types page of a project.

See the Default, Create, Edit and View screen of every issue type. You see at once which screens you can edit and which are shared with other projects.

 #EAF2FF :mag:

Preview before every save

"What happens on save" lists every change before it runs.

Edit screens with drag and drop, change which screen an issue type uses, or copy a screen as a template. You see exactly what will change, and you can undo it.

 #E9F7EF :white_check_mark:

Keep the configuration clean

The Health page with one-click fixes.

The health check finds create screens without Summary, invisible fields, out-of-date names and empty tabs. Unused screens the app created can be cleaned up automatically.

Who it is for

 #FFF4EE :busts_in_silhouette:

Project admins

You have the Administer Projects permission for a company-managed project. You use the app every day to:

  • add, remove and reorder fields and tabs on your screens
  • decide which screen each issue type uses
  • set up transition screens for your workflows
  • fix problems and tidy up unused screens

Read the User guide.

 #EAF2FF :gear:

Jira admins

You have the Administer Jira permission. You install the app and decide:

  • which projects may use it
  • whether screens can be copied from other projects
  • whether unused screens are deleted automatically
  • how long the audit log is kept, and whether AI features are on

Read the Admin guide.

Explore the documentation

title: Screen Self-Service – Getting started
body:
For Jira admins and project admins who are new to the app. You will install Screen Self-Service for Jira, see what Jira asks you to approve, and make your first screen change.

 2

Before you start

What you need

  • Jira Cloud.
  • Company-managed projects that use field schemes. Team-managed projects have no screens, so the app does not work there. Sites that still use the older field configurations are not supported yet.
  • A Jira admin to install the app. After that, project admins can use it on their own.

Install the app

A Jira admin does this once for the whole site.

  1. Open Screen Self-Service for Jira on the Atlassian Marketplace. You can also search for "Screen Self-Service" under Apps in Jira.
  2. Start the installation and choose your Jira site.
  3. Review the permissions Jira shows you (see the next section) and confirm.
  4. Wait for the message that the app is installed.

The app is free for sites with up to 10 users. Larger sites get a 30-day free trial. After that, the price per user drops as your company grows. You see the exact price on the Marketplace listing.

What Jira asks you to approve, and why

During the installation, Jira lists the permissions the app needs. Here is what each one is used for, in plain words.

PermissionWhy the app needs it
Read Jira project and configuration dataTo show your project's issue types, screens, screen schemes, workflows and fields, and to plan a change before it runs.
Read user informationTo check the permissions of the person using the app before every action, and to show names in the audit log. Only account IDs are stored.
Manage projectsTo change your own project's setup, for example which screen scheme an issue type uses, or to add a field to the project's field scheme.
Manage Jira configurationIn Jira, screens and screen schemes are site settings. Creating, editing, renaming and deleting them needs this permission, even though the app only touches objects that your project alone uses.
Store app dataTo keep the app's own data in Atlassian's cloud: settings, the audit log, undo records and the list of objects the app created.

The app never does more than the person using it may do in Jira. Every action checks that person's real permissions first. Details: Security & privacy.

Where to find the app in Jira

 #FFF4EE :busts_in_silhouette:

Project admins

Open your company-managed project, then Project settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira.

 #EAF2FF :gear:

Jira admins

Open Jira settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira for the app's Configuration and the site-wide Audit log.

Your first steps

1. Jira admin: choose the settings (optional)

Open Jira settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira. By default, every project may use the app, copying screens from other projects is on, automatic clean-up is off, and AI features are off. Change what you need and choose Save. See the Admin guide.

2. Project admin: open the app

Go to Project settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira. While the app shows Getting your screens ready, it checks three things:

  • Company-managed project
  • Uses field schemes
  • You administer this project

If one of them is not true, the app tells you why. See the FAQ.

3. Look at your screens

The Issue types page shows each issue type with its Default, Create, Edit and View screen.

The Issue types page: an orange dot means editable, a lock means shared with other projects.

4. Make a small change

  1. Find an issue type marked Only plus your project key (for example Only PROJ) and choose Edit on one of its screens.
  2. Find a field under Add field and choose +, or drag a field to a new position.
  3. Choose Save.

The screen editor: fields on the left, Add field on the right.

5. Check it, and undo if you like

Open the Audit log tab: your change is listed there. Choose Undo in the header (or press Ctrl+Z / ⌘Z) to take it back. Undo works for your last change within 24 hours.

You're done when…

#E9F7EF :white_check_mark:
  • The app opens under Project settings → Apps without a notice.
  • You see your issue types and their screens on the Issue types page.
  • Your test change appears in the Audit log.
  • Your project admins know where to find the app and this documentation.

Next: the User guide for everyday tasks.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Screen Self-Service – User guide
body:
For project admins of company-managed projects. Learn how to edit, assign, copy and clean up the screens of your project, and how to undo a change.

 2

Open the app

  1. Open your company-managed project in Jira.
  2. Go to Project settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira.
  3. The app checks that the project is company-managed, uses field schemes, and that you have the Administer Projects permission. Then it opens the Issue types page.

The tabs at the top are Issue types, Health, Transition screens, Unused and Audit log. The buttons Copy screen and New screen are always in the header.

A screen decides which fields people see when they create, edit or view an issue. In Jira, each issue type has a screen for Default, Create, Edit and View. If an operation has no screen of its own, it uses the Default screen ("inherits from Default").

Read the Issue types page

Each card shows one screen scheme with its issue types, and the screen used for each operation.

Issue types page: Bug uses its own screens, Epic uses screens shared with 24 projects.

You seeIt means
Editable (orange dot), Only PROJOnly your project uses this. You can change it.
Shared, read only (lock), Shared · 24 projectsOther projects use it too. You can look, but not change it.
inherits from DefaultThis operation uses the Default screen.

Each screen card has a small state map: the Default state on top, Create, Edit and View below. A filled box means the screen is used for that state. An outlined box means another screen handles it. Point at the map (or focus it with the keyboard) to see which screen each state uses.

Find out why a screen is locked

  1. On a shared card, choose Why locked?
  2. Under How PROJ reaches this screen you see the path from the screen to your project, and which other projects use it. Choose Show projects for the full list.
  3. Under Need a change? choose Copy name to send the screen name to your Jira admin, or Make a copy for PROJ to get your own version.

A shared screen shows how your project reaches it and which projects share it.

Shared screens and schemes are always read-only for project admins. A change would apply to every project that uses them.

Edit a screen

  1. On an editable screen, choose Edit.
  2. Drag a field to reorder it. To move it to another tab, drop it on that tab's name.
  3. To add a field, type in Find a field and choose + next to it.
  4. To remove a field, choose × next to it.
  5. Use Add tab, Tab name and Remove tab to manage tabs.
  6. Choose Save (or press Ctrl+S / ⌘S). Discard drops your unsaved changes.

The screen editor with tabs, fields and the Add field list.

A field marked not yet in field scheme is added to your project's field scheme when you save, so it really shows up on issues. This only works when the field scheme belongs to your project alone.
  • Required fields such as Summary and Issue type show Can't be removed.
  • If the field scheme is shared with other projects, new fields must already be in it. Ask your Jira admin to add them.
  • The Usage box shows which issue types and operations use this screen.

Change which screen an issue type uses

  1. On an editable card, choose Change assignment.
  2. For each operation (Default, Create, Edit, View), choose a screen. You can also pick New screen, Copy another screen… or Inherit from Default.
  3. Read What happens on save. It lists every rename, new screen and changed assignment.
  4. Choose Save.

Change assignment: pick a screen per operation and check the preview before you save.

What the preview shows is exactly what runs. If Jira changed in the meantime, the app refuses, loads the latest state and asks you to check again.

Give an issue type its own screens, or merge issue types

When several issue types share one screen scheme, a change affects all of them.

Split off an issue type

  1. On the card, choose Split off issue type.
  2. Under Which issue type gets split off? pick the issue type.
  3. Under How does … start? choose Copy screens (recommended: the issue type gets its own copies) or Keep using the same screens (it only gets its own screen scheme).
  4. Check What happens and confirm.

Merge issue types

  1. On the card, choose Merge.
  2. Pick which issue type moves, and which screens it should use from now on. Only screen schemes that your project alone uses are offered.
  3. Check Before and after. Objects nothing uses any more are listed under Becomes free and move to Unused.
  4. Choose Merge.

Create a new screen

  1. Choose New screen in the header.
  2. Choose the issue type and operation the screen is for.
  3. Choose Create and edit. A new create screen starts with Summary and Issue Type.

Copy a screen as a template

  1. Choose Copy screen in the header.
  2. Under Pick a template, search by name. Screens of your project appear first, then All screens on the site.
  3. Check the Preview on the right. The original stays untouched.
  4. Choose the Issue type and Assign as (Default, Create, Edit or View). The Name of the copy is filled in for you.
  5. Choose Copy and edit.

Copy a screen: search, preview, choose where it applies, then copy.

If you see Copying from other projects is off, your Jira admin has limited copying to your own project's screens.

Add or remove fields on many screens

  1. On the Issue types page, choose Change fields on many screens.
  2. Under What should happen? choose Add fields or Remove fields.
  3. Under Which fields? pick one or more fields.
  4. Under On which screens? pick screens, or use a preset: All screens, Create, Edit, View, Create + Edit.
  5. Under Into which tab? choose First tab or Tab named. A named tab is created on screens that don't have it yet.
  6. Check the Preview for each screen and choose Apply to … screens.

Change fields on several screens, with a preview per screen.

Shared screens are skipped automatically (Shared with other projects — skipped). Required fields are kept.

Set up a transition screen

A transition screen pops up when someone moves an issue from one status to another, for example to ask for a reason.

  1. Open the Transition screens tab.
  2. Under New transition screen, type the middle part of the name (for example "Approval") and choose Create. The screen is named like "PROJ Transition - Approval - Screen".
  3. Choose Edit to add fields.
  4. Choose Assign and switch the screen on for the transitions where it should pop up.

Transition screens of a project, with the workflows and transitions that use them.

You can only change transition screens when every workflow that uses them belongs to your project alone. Inactive workflows and drafts count too. Otherwise the screen shows Read only.

Fix problems with the Health check

If the app finds problems, a banner such as 1 configuration issue found appears on the Issue types page. Choose Review, or open the Health tab.

The Health page lists what to look at and offers a fix for each problem.

CheckWhy it mattersWhat you can do
Create screens without SummaryIssues of these types cannot be created.Fix puts Summary at the top of the first tab.
Fields that are invisibleThe fields are on your screens but not in the field scheme, so nobody sees them.Fix adds them to the field scheme.
Names out of syncNames no longer follow the naming scheme.Fix renames them.
Empty transition screensUsers see an empty dialog on a transition.Review opens Transition screens: add fields or switch the screen off.
Empty tabsThey show up as empty sections.Fix removes them.
Unused screens and schemesNothing uses them any more.Review opens the Unused tab.

Choose Fix all to run every available fix. Each fix can be undone. A problem marked Needs your Jira admin involves something shared with other projects.

Clean up unused screens

The Unused tab lists screens and screen schemes that nothing in your project uses any more.

  1. Open the Unused tab.
  2. To keep an object, choose Assign again. This also cancels its deletion.
  3. To delete it, press and hold Hold to delete (or click it twice).

Unused objects with a countdown to their automatic deletion.

  • You can only delete objects the app created. Others show Not created by this app. Only your Jira admin can delete it.
  • If your Jira admin turned on automatic deletion, the Deletion column shows the date.
  • Deleted something by mistake? Undo brings it back with all its tabs and fields.

Undo a change

Choose Undo in the header or in the message after saving, or press Ctrl+Z / ⌘Z. This reverts your last change in the project, including deletions, for 24 hours.

Undo only runs if Jira still looks exactly as it did right after your change. If someone changed the same objects since, the app refuses and changes nothing.

See who changed what

The Audit log tab lists every change made through the app in your project: what changed, who made it and when. Use Filter the log to search. Open an entry to see Before and After.

The audit log, grouped by day.

Jump anywhere with Ctrl+K

Press Ctrl+K / ⌘K, or choose Search or jump to…, to open the command palette. Type a screen, issue type or action and press Enter.

The command palette with actions and screens. The Rovo section appears only when AI features are on.

The palette also has Toggle dark mode and a language switch (Deutsch / English). The app starts in your Jira language and theme.

Ask the Screen Assistant (Rovo)

The Screen Assistant is off by default. It is only available when Rovo is enabled for your site and a Jira admin has turned on AI features (Rovo agent). Until then, the app shows no Ask Rovo button.

Open it from Ask Rovo in the app or from Rovo chat. The agent can:

  • list which screens your project uses
  • explain a screen, including why it is locked
  • find unused screens and their deletion dates
  • add a field to, or remove a field from, a screen of your project. It asks you to confirm first.

The agent follows the same permission and safety rules as the app. AI answers can be wrong, so check them before you rely on them.

How the app names screens

The app keeps names consistent, so you can tell at a glance what a screen is for:

  • Screens: KEY IssueType - operations - Screen, for example PROJ Bug - create, edit - Screen
  • Screen schemes: KEY IssueType - Screen Scheme
  • Transition screens: KEY Transition - name - Screen

Names follow the current assignment and update automatically when it changes. The preview always shows renames before you save.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Screen Self-Service – Admin guide
body:
For Jira admins. Learn how to set up Screen Self-Service for Jira for your site: which projects may use it, clean-up, audit log, AI features, licence and maintenance.

 2

Open the configuration

Go to Jira settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira. The page has two tabs:

  • Configuration – all settings of the app
  • Audit log – every change made through the app, on all projects

Change one or more settings, then choose Save in the bar at the bottom. Discard drops your unsaved changes. The app confirms with Configuration saved.

As a Jira admin you can also do everything a project admin can, in any project: open Project settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira in that project.

Settings at a glance

SettingWhat it doesDefault
Projects that can use the appAll projects, or only the Selected projects you list by key. Jira admins can always use the app.GreenAll projects
Copy screens from other projectsLets project admins search every screen on the site and copy it into their project as a template.GreenOn
Delete unused screens and screen schemes automaticallyDeletes objects created by the app after they have been unused for the number of days you choose.GreyOff (suggested: 30 days)
Audit log retentionDeletes older audit entries automatically.Blue24 months
AI features (Rovo agent)Turns the Rovo agent "Screen Assistant" and every Ask Rovo entry point on or off.GreyOff
Shared screens and schemesAlways Locked, with a notice. Project admins can't edit objects other projects also use, but they can copy them.GreyFixed

Choose which projects can use the app

  1. Under Projects that can use the app, choose All projects or Selected projects.
  2. For selected projects, type the Project keys, separated by commas (for example PROJ, SUP, HR).
  3. Choose Save.

If you choose Selected projects and list no key, only Jira admins can use the app. Text that isn't a valid project key is shown as Not a project key, and you can't save until you fix it. Check the keys carefully: the app checks their format, so a typo that looks like a key is accepted.

Allow or stop copying screens from other projects

With Copy screens from other projects on, project admins can search every screen on the site by name and copy it into their project. The original is never changed. Turn it off to limit them to their own project's screens; they then see Copying from other projects is off.

Clean up unused screens automatically

  1. Under Delete unused screens and screen schemes automatically, switch Active on.
  2. Set Delete after … days unused with the buttons or a quick pick (14, 30, 60 or 90). You can choose 1 to 365 days.
  3. Choose Save.
  • This only affects screens and screen schemes created by the app. Anything else is never deleted by the app.
  • Project admins see the deletion date for each object on their Unused tab. Assigning an object again cancels its deletion.
  • The clean-up runs once a night. Every deletion is written to the audit log as "Screen Self-Service for Jira (auto-deletion)".

Set how long the audit log is kept

Under Audit log retention, choose 12 months, 24 months, 36 months or Never (keep everything). Older entries are deleted automatically every night.

Turn AI features on or off

The app includes a Rovo agent called Screen Assistant. It can list a project's screens, explain a screen, find unused screens, and add or remove a field (after the user confirms). It follows the same permission and safety rules as the app.

SwitchWhat happens
GreyOff (default)All Ask Rovo buttons and Rovo prompts in the Ctrl+K palette are hidden. The agent refuses every request and tells the user where a Jira admin can turn it on.
GreenOnProject admins can use the Screen Assistant. Rovo must also be enabled for your site.

AI results can be wrong and must be reviewed. If you see Temporarily turned off by the app vendor, SUPERPORT has paused the AI features for all sites. Your setting is kept and applies again once AI is available.

Permissions: who can do what

WhoJira permissionWhat they can do in the app
Project adminAdminister Projects for the projectManage the screens, screen schemes and transition screens that belong to their project alone, if the project may use the app.
Jira adminAdminister JiraEverything a project admin can, in any project, plus the configuration and the site-wide audit log.
Everyone else–No access. The app shows Only project admins can manage screens.

The app checks these permissions in Jira on every action. It never does more than the person using it may do.

  • Screens, schemes and workflows used by other projects are read-only. This is checked again against live Jira data right before every change.
  • If Jira can't confirm that an object belongs to one project only, the app changes nothing.
  • Only objects the app created can be deleted, and only when unused. Other unused objects can only be deleted by a Jira admin.

There is no separate approval step. Project admins see a preview and the change runs when they save. You stay in control through the project list, the copy switch and the audit log, and every change can be undone for 24 hours.

Review the audit log

Open the Audit log tab on the configuration page. It lists every change made through the app on all projects, including configuration changes and automatic deletions. Use Filter the log to search, and open an entry to see Before and After.

The audit log shows who changed what, and when.

  • The log stores account IDs only. Names are looked up when you open the log.
  • When an account is closed, its entries show Former user.

Licence

  • The app is free for sites with up to 10 users. Larger sites get a 30-day free trial, then a per-user subscription billed through Atlassian.
  • Without an active licence, the app shows Screen Self-Service for Jira needs an active license and changes nothing. Your Jira screens and everything you set up keep working as usual.
  • To start a trial or renew, go to Apps → Manage apps in Jira.

Maintenance and status

In rare cases, SUPERPORT pauses the app to keep your data safe, for example during an incident. Users then see one of these notices:

NoticeWhat it means
YellowRead-only Changes are paused for maintenance to keep your data safe.Everyone can still view everything. Editing comes back as soon as possible.
RedUnder maintenance Screen Self-Service for Jira is temporarily unavailableThe app is paused. Nothing saved is lost, and your Jira screens keep working.

Follow updates on the SUPERPORT Apps status page.

Data export and uninstall

The app has no data export. Screens and schemes created through the app are normal Jira configuration and stay in Jira if you uninstall the app. The app's own data (settings, audit log, undo records) is deleted by Atlassian after uninstall. See Security & privacy.

Large sites and platform limits

The app runs on Atlassian Forge, which limits compute time, storage and API requests for all apps.

  • On large sites, the overview of where screens and schemes are used can take a moment to build.
  • When Jira answers "too many requests", the app slows down and retries by itself, so a change may take longer.
  • If a limit is still reached, the app shows an error. The audit log shows which changes were applied. Try the rest again a little later.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Screen Self-Service – FAQ & troubleshooting
body:
For project admins and Jira admins. Find answers to common questions and learn what to do when the app shows a message. Choose a question to open the answer.

 2

Opening the app

I can't find the app in my project.

Look under Project settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira. You need the Administer Projects permission to see project settings. If the entry is missing, ask your Jira admin whether the app is installed on your site.

 "Team-managed projects have no screens"

Your project is team-managed. Team-managed projects set up fields directly in the issue type and don't use screens, so the app can't help there. It works with company-managed projects.

 "This site still uses field configurations"

The app needs field schemes. Your site still uses the older field configurations, which the app does not support yet. Once your Jira admin has migrated the site, the app works without any further setup.

 "Only project admins can manage screens" or "You need the "Administer Projects" permission for this project"

You are not a project admin of this project. Ask a project admin or your Jira admin to give you the Administer Projects permission, for example by adding you to the project's administrators role.

 "Your Jira admin has not enabled Screen Self-Service for Jira for this project."

Your Jira admin has limited the app to selected projects. Ask them to add your project key under Projects that can use the app on the app's configuration page.

Locked and shared screens

Why is a screen locked?

Another project uses it too (Also used by … other projects). A change would apply to all of them, so the app doesn't let you edit it. Choose Why locked? to see how your project reaches the screen and which projects share it. Then choose Make a copy for your project to get your own version, or Copy name and send it to your Jira admin.

 A transition screen shows "Read only". Why?

At least one workflow that uses it is shared with another project. Transition screens are only editable when every workflow using them belongs to your project alone. Inactive workflows and drafts count too.

 "Copying from other projects is off" or "Your Jira admin has turned off copying screens from other projects."

Your Jira admin has turned off Copy screens from other projects. You can still copy your own project's screens. Ask your Jira admin if you need a screen from another project.

Editing and saving

I added a field to a screen, but nobody sees it on issues.

The field is probably missing from your project's field scheme. Open the Health tab: Fields that are invisible lists these fields, and Fix adds them to the field scheme. If you see The field scheme is shared — ask your Jira admin to add these fields first, other projects use the same field scheme, so only your Jira admin can add the field.

 Why can't I remove Summary or Issue type?

They are required fields. Without them, issues can't be created, so the editor shows Can't be removed.

 "Jira changed since your preview. The latest state has been loaded — please review and confirm again."

Someone changed the same configuration after you opened the preview. To be safe, the app did not save anything. Check the new preview and save again. You may also see Jira changed in the meantime or This screen was changed elsewhere while you were editing: the same applies, redo your change on the latest version.

 The names of my screens changed by themselves.

The app keeps names in line with how screens are used, for example PROJ Bug - create, edit - Screen. When you change an assignment, names update with it. The preview under What happens on save always lists renames before you save. The Audit log shows every rename.

 "This Jira site has more workflows than the app can check safely. Nothing was changed."

Before every change, the app checks that nothing it touches is used by another project. On this site it couldn't complete that check, so it changed nothing to stay safe. Contact us through the support portal so we can look at it with you.

 A change takes long, or I see "Something went wrong" or "Unexpected error. The change was not completed".

Atlassian limits how many requests an app can send to Jira. When Jira answers "too many requests", the app slows down and retries by itself. If a limit is still reached, you see an error. Check the Audit log to see which changes were applied, and try the rest again a little later.

For any other error, reload the page and try again. Completed changes are always listed in the Audit log. If it happens again, contact us through the support portal and tell us what you did and when.

Undo and deleting

"This change can no longer be undone: the affected objects were changed since. Nothing was reverted."

Undo only runs if Jira still looks exactly as it did right after your change. Someone changed the same objects after you, so undo would overwrite their work. Make the change you need by hand instead. Undo also only covers your last change, for 24 hours.

 I can't delete an unused screen.
  • Not created by this app. Only your Jira admin can delete it. The app only deletes screens and schemes it created itself.
  • in … — delete that first: the screen is still part of an unused screen scheme. Delete the screen scheme first.
 A screen I still need is about to be deleted automatically.

Open the Unused tab and choose Assign again. Using the object again cancels its deletion. If it was already deleted, Undo brings it back with all its tabs and fields (within 24 hours).

Licence and availability

"Screen Self-Service for Jira needs an active license"

The licence for your site isn't active, for example because the trial ended or the subscription was cancelled. The app changes nothing until it is active again. Your Jira screens keep working as usual. A Jira admin can start a trial or renew under Apps → Manage apps.

 "Temporarily unavailable" or "Changes are paused for maintenance"

SUPERPORT has paused the app, or made it read-only, to keep your data safe. Nothing you saved is lost, and your Jira screens keep working. Follow the progress on the status page and try again later.

Rovo and AI

I don't see "Ask Rovo", or the Screen Assistant says "AI features of this app are turned off".

AI features are off by default. A Jira admin turns them on under Jira settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira → AI features (Rovo agent). Rovo must also be enabled for your site. If you see Rovo opens inside Jira once Rovo is enabled for your site, Rovo itself isn't available yet.

If the Screen Assistant says the features are temporarily turned off by the app vendor, SUPERPORT has paused them for all sites. Please try again later.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Screen Self-Service – Security & privacy
body:
For Jira admins, security and privacy teams. Learn what data Screen Self-Service for Jira stores, where it stays, which permissions it needs, and how it protects your configuration.

 2

At a glance

 #E9F7EF :cloud:

Runs on Atlassian

The app runs entirely on Atlassian Forge. It has no external connections, no third-party services and no analytics.

 #EAF2FF :lock:

Your data stays in your site

Everything is kept in the Forge storage of your installation. SUPERPORT does not receive your data. Data residency follows your Jira site.

 #FFF4EE :shield:

Never more than you may do

Every action re-checks the user's real Jira permissions. Configuration shared with other projects is never changed.

What the app stores

All data is kept in Atlassian's Forge hosted storage, per installation.

DataContentsPersonal data?Kept for
SettingsAutomatic clean-up on/off and days, audit retention, allowed project keys, copy switch, AI switchNoUntil changed or the app is uninstalled
Audit logTime, account ID of the person who made the change, action, object name, short before/after summaryAccount ID only. Names are not stored; they are looked up when the log is shown.24 months by default. A Jira admin can choose 12, 24 or 36 months, or never delete. Older entries are deleted nightly.
Undo recordsSnapshot of the screens and schemes touched by a user's last changeAccount ID (as part of the key)24 hours, then deleted nightly
Created-objects listIDs of screens and schemes the app created, and when they became unusedNoUntil the object is deleted or the app is uninstalled
Privacy job markerTime of the last personal-data reportNoOverwritten weekly
#F4F5F7 :no_entry_sign:

What the app does not store

  • issue content or issue data
  • attachments or comments
  • email addresses
  • user profile data
 #F4F5F7 :outbox_tray:

What leaves Atlassian

Nothing. The app makes no calls to external hosts, and its interface loads no files from outside. There are no sub-processors besides Atlassian.

Permissions (scopes) and why the app needs them

ScopeWhy
read:jira-workRead the project, its issue types, screens, screen schemes, workflows and fields to show the overview and plan changes.
read:jira-userCheck the signed-in user's own permissions before every action, and show names in the audit log (only account IDs are stored).
manage:jira-projectChange the configuration of the user's own project: which screen scheme each issue type uses, and fields added to the project's field scheme. Only after confirming the user has Administer Projects for that project.
manage:jira-configurationScreens, screen schemes and workflow transition screens are site configuration in Jira. Creating, editing, renaming and deleting them needs this scope, even though the app only changes objects used by the user's own project.
storage:appKeep the app's own data in Atlassian's Forge storage: settings, audit log, undo records and the list of objects the app created.

How the app keeps your configuration safe

  • Trusted identity. The user and project come only from Atlassian's signed context, never from what the browser sends.
  • Real permission checks. Every request checks the user's Jira permissions: Administer Projects for project pages, Administer Jira for the configuration. The Rovo agent checks the same way.
  • Only your project. Right before every write, the app reloads Jira's current state and checks that every screen, scheme and workflow it touches belongs to that project alone. Shared objects are refused.
  • Fails closed. If any read fails or is incomplete, the app writes nothing.
  • Safe deletion. Only objects the app created, and only when unused. Every deletion can be undone for 24 hours.
  • No cross-project leaks. Keys of projects a user can't browse are removed from everything the app and the Rovo agent show.
  • Licence and maintenance. Without an active licence, the app changes nothing. During an incident, SUPERPORT can make the app read-only or unavailable; users see a notice and a link to the status page.
  • Encryption. In transit and at rest, provided by Atlassian Forge.

Personal data

  • The only personal data the app stores are the Atlassian account IDs of users who change screens through the app (audit log and undo records).
  • The app uses Atlassian's Personal Data Reporting API. A weekly job reports stored account IDs to Atlassian. For closed accounts, audit entries are changed to "Former user" and their undo records are deleted.
  • You (the customer) are the controller of this data. SUPERPORT doesn't receive it; the app processes it only inside your Atlassian site.
  • A Jira admin sets how long the audit log is kept. On request, SUPERPORT support can explain how to remove specific entries.

AI features

  • The Rovo agent "Screen Assistant" is off by default, also for existing installations. A Jira admin turns it on under AI features (Rovo agent).
  • While it is off, the app hides every Ask Rovo entry point and the agent refuses every request.
  • When it is on, the agent follows the same permission and safety rules as the app, and asks the user to confirm before any change.
  • SUPERPORT can turn AI features off for all sites, for example during an incident.

Retention and uninstall

When you uninstall the app, Atlassian soft-deletes its Forge storage and deletes it permanently after the retention period (currently 28 days, see Atlassian's hosted storage data lifecycle). Within the first 21 days, you can ask Atlassian to recover it.

Screens and schemes created through the app belong to your Jira and stay after uninstall.

Report a security issue

  • Please report security issues privately by email to mail@superport.digital with the subject "Security: Screen Self-Service for Jira". Please don't open a public issue.
  • We confirm receipt within two business days and keep you informed until it is resolved.
  • SUPERPORT notifies affected customers of a security incident without undue delay, and within 72 hours where GDPR applies.
  • Status and incident updates: superapps.statuspage.io

Legal

Use of the app is governed by the SUPERPORT App EULA & privacy policy. Vendor: SUPERPORT P.C., Athens, Greece, www.superport.digital.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.

title: Screen Self-Service – Release notes
body:
For everyone who uses or manages the app. See what changed in each release, newest first. Screen Self-Service for Jira updates automatically on your site; you don't need to do anything.

Version 5.7.0 – 16 November 2026

GreenNEW AI features switch. Jira admins now decide whether the Rovo agent "Screen Assistant" can be used, with AI features (Rovo agent) on the configuration page.

  • AI features are off by default, also on sites that already had the app installed.
  • While they are off, the app hides every Ask Rovo button and the Rovo prompts in the Ctrl+K / ⌘K palette.
  • The Screen Assistant then refuses every request and tells users where a Jira admin can turn it on.
  • SUPERPORT can pause AI features for all sites if needed. Your setting is kept and applies again afterwards.

Want to keep using the Screen Assistant? Turn on AI features (Rovo agent) under Jira settings → Apps → Screen Self-Service for Jira. See the Admin guide.

13 November 2026

BlueIMPROVED State map on screen cards. Each screen card on the Issue types page now shows a small map of the Default, Create, Edit and View states instead of a tab thumbnail.

  • A filled box means the screen is used for that state (directly, or by inheriting from Default). An outlined box means another screen handles it.
  • Point at the map, or focus it with the keyboard, to see which screen each state uses.
  • Pointing at a box highlights the matching card, and pointing at a card highlights its box.

The state map on the right of each screen card shows which states use the screen.

GreyDOCS The documentation now explains the state map and Atlassian's platform limits (for example, automatic retries when Jira reports too many requests).

First Marketplace release – 5 November 2026

GreenNEW Screen Self-Service for Jira is available on the Atlassian Marketplace. Project admins of company-managed projects can manage their own screens:

  • Overview of every issue type with its Default, Create, Edit and View screen, and which screens are editable, shared or inherited.
  • Drag-and-drop screen editor for fields and tabs. Missing fields are added to the project's field scheme automatically.
  • Change which screen an issue type uses, with a plain-language preview before every save.
  • Split an issue type off a shared screen scheme, or merge issue types.
  • New screens, and copies of any screen on the site as a template.
  • Change fields on many screens at once.
  • Transition screens for workflows only your project uses.
  • Health check with one-click fixes, and clean-up of unused screens with an optional automatic deletion.
  • Undo for the last change (24 hours), and a full audit log.
  • Rovo agent "Screen Assistant".
  • Ctrl+K / ⌘K command palette, English and German, light and dark theme.

Shared screens and schemes stay locked, with the reason shown. Every request re-checks the user's real Jira permissions. The app runs on Atlassian and sends no data outside it.

Need help? Contact us through the SUPERPORT support portal.
